You Shouldn't Let ChatGPT Write Your Emails

Released Aug 4, 2026, 17 min

Play You Shouldn't Let ChatGPT Write Your Emails on YouTube
Watch on YouTube

Is it morally wrong to send emails that are mostly written by AI?

In this episode, I argue that the answer is often yes.

Rather than debating whether large language models are "good" or "bad" in general, I focus on a much narrower claim: sending emails that are primarily generated by an LLM is frequently a moral mistake.

I develop two arguments:

  • It can involve a kind of deception by presenting AI-generated words as your own communication.
  • It can be selfish and anti-relational by offloading the effort of communication while expecting others to engage with the result.

Along the way I discuss changing social norms around AI, whether widespread AI use changes the ethics, and why authenticity still matters even in an age of increasingly capable language models.

I also explain where I think AI use is perfectly appropriate—for editing, brainstorming, improving clarity, generating metadata, standardizing formats, and other cases where it genuinely serves the reader rather than replacing the human author.
